fact: Waters Edge's design guidelines require Design Review Committee approval before any artificial turf is installed, bar it from front yards, and hold it at least 2 feet off every lot line behind a buffer of rock or other approved material, screened by landscaping from neighboring lots, streets and common areas.
quote: Approval from the DRC is required prior to any installation of artificial turf. • Artificial turf may NOT be installed in front yard landscapes • Artificial turf must be installed a minimum of 2’ off of all lot lines and must be separated from lot lines and fences along lot lines by a buffer of rock or other approved landscape materials, and must be screened by landscaping in order to minimize the visual impact from the ground level of adjacent lots, streets or any common area tracts.
source_label: Waters Edge Metropolitan District Design Guidelines (Sonders Fort Collins), Sec. III.a Artificial Turf, as posted on the district's Design Guidelines page
notes: Downloaded with curl and read with pdftotext 2026-09-26. The cover says the guidelines were adopted by the Board of Waters' Edge Metropolitan District No. 1, 2; the adoption date on the cover is blank. The posted file name starts 061825 (probably June 18, 2025, not stated in the document).

fact: A Waters Edge turf request must include a plan of the turf area and its drainage, a 12-by-12-inch sample with the manufacturer's product and component information and any use warnings, and turf with a weight of at least 60 ounces.
quote: Adequate base/drainage must be provided under the turf surface, and a plan showing the turf installation area and proposed drainage plan must be provided with the design review submission. • A 12” X 12” sample of the proposed artificial turf, together with product name, manufacturer, and component information supplied by the manufacturer, along with any material or use warnings that apply to the product must be provided with the design review submission. • Weight must be at minimum 60 ounce.
source_label: Waters Edge Metropolitan District Design Guidelines (Sonders Fort Collins), Sec. III.a Artificial Turf, as posted on the district's Design Guidelines page
notes: The guidelines do not say whether the 60-ounce weight is face weight or total weight, or per what area.

fact: Approved turf at Waters Edge must be kept from fading, cracking or falling into disrepair, or the owner can be required to replace it with new product or with natural turf.
quote: If approved, artificial turf must be maintained in an attractive condition, and not allowed to fade, crack, or otherwise fall into disrepair. If artificial turf is not maintained in accordance with community standards, the homeowner will be required to remove and replace the artificial turf with new product or with natural turf.
source_label: Waters Edge Metropolitan District Design Guidelines (Sonders Fort Collins), Sec. III.a Artificial Turf, as posted on the district's Design Guidelines page

fact: Waters Edge's guidelines list putting greens with sandboxes and playhouses as play equipment that needs no Design Review Committee approval if it is no more than 4 feet high, sits in the back yard at least 6 feet from any property line and is kept in good repair.
quote: Play equipment such as sandboxes, playhouses and tents, and putting greens shall not require approval of the DRC provided that such equipment is not more than four (4) feet high and in good repair (including painting) and located in the back yard and a minimum or six (6) feet from any property line
source_label: Waters Edge Metropolitan District Design Guidelines (Sonders Fort Collins), Sec. III.m Play Equipment Generally
notes: Sec. III.a separately requires DRC approval 'prior to any installation of artificial turf'. The guidelines do not say which clause governs a synthetic putting green; the page says so and sends owners to the DRC.

fact: Waters Edge requires Design Review Committee approval before work starts on landscaping the builder did not install, on substantial changes to approved landscaping including xeriscaping, and on added structures such as patios, fencing, lighting, hot tubs and pools.
quote: Design Review Committee (DRC) review and approval are required prior to commencing work and in accordance with the Declaration for the following: a) Initial landscape not installed by the builder b) Substantial modifications to previously approved landscape designs and installations, including xeriscaping c) Addition of structures to the property including decks/patios, arbors, awnings, overhangs, exterior home additions or changes, fencing, lighting, gazebos, greenhouses, sunrooms, hot tubs, spas, saunas, pools, pet enclosures/houses, renewable energy generation devices, and trampolines
source_label: Waters Edge Metropolitan District Design Guidelines (Sonders Fort Collins), Sec. II Design Review Requirements

fact: The Waters Edge Design Review Committee normally meets once a month and may take up to 45 days to answer; a request needs a plot plan, the lot and block numbers and lot square footage, and attached photographs rather than internet links, and incomplete applications are returned.
quote: Plans and specifications should be detailed and include the following: • Plot plan showing the location of the Improvement(s) • Lot #, Block # and square footage of Lot … No links to internet sites are permitted, photographs must be attached … • Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant PLAN AHEAD! The DRC strives to respond to requests quickly, however, the Design Review Committee normally meets once per month … and it may take up to 45 days after the submittal is received for a response to be sent to an applicant.
source_label: Waters Edge Metropolitan District Design Guidelines (Sonders Fort Collins), Sec. IV Application Submittal, Processing, Inspection, and Enforcement

fact: Waters Edge design requests go on the form on the district's website to the district manager, who forwards them to the Design Review Committee and returns its written decision: approved, approved with conditions, denied pending more information, or denied.
quote: Please use the submittal form on the Metropolitan District’s website to coordinate all information. Requests for approval should be mailed or emailed to the District Manager (address and email are on the submittal form and on the District's website). The District Manager will forward requests to the DRC Committee, track them through the submittal process and return written information to applicants regarding the Design Review Committee’s decision. Decisions will be mailed in written format and will be one of four responses: • Approved • Approved with conditions • Denied - Request for additional information • Denied
source_label: Waters Edge Metropolitan District Design Guidelines (Sonders Fort Collins), Sec. IV Application Submittal, Processing, Inspection, and Enforcement

fact: A Waters Edge approval lapses if the work is not finished within 12 months unless the committee extends it; after a written notice of completion the committee may inspect for 90 days, and a noncompliance finding must be corrected, or appealed to the district board, within 45 days.
quote: If the Improvement is not completed within twelve (12) months after the date of approval, or such shorter period as specified by the DRC, the approval shall automatically lapse; provided, however, the DRC may, in its discretion, grant extensions of time for completion of any proposed Improvement. … Upon completion of an Improvement, the applicant shall give written “Notice of Completion” to the DRC. … The right of inspection shall terminate ninety (90) days after the DRC has received Notice of Completion from the applicant. … the applicant must fully correct all noncompliance within forth-five (45) days after receipt of such notice, provided that the applicant may appeal such determination to the Metropolitan District’s Board of Directors by giving written notice of such appeal to the Metropolitan District’s Board of Directors and the DRC within forty-five (45) days after receipt of notice of noncompliance.
source_label: Waters Edge Metropolitan District Design Guidelines (Sonders Fort Collins), Sec. IV.a to IV.d

fact: Under the Waters Edge guidelines, an improvement installed without approval can be removed at the owner's expense, and the district board may add fines or other legal action.
quote: Any Improvement installed without approval is subject to removal at the Owner’s sole expense. The Owner may also be subject to fines or other legal action, to be determined by the Metropolitan District’s Board of Directors at its discretion.
source_label: Waters Edge Metropolitan District Design Guidelines (Sonders Fort Collins), Sec. IV Application Submittal, Processing, Inspection, and Enforcement

fact: At Waters Edge the builder installs each parkway strip as natural turf with City-designated trees, and an owner who wants to xeriscape it needs Design Review Committee approval first and then a Fort Collins parkway landscape amendment.
quote: Parkway strips (the area between the sidewalk and street) are required to be installed by the applicable builder as part of the front yard landscaping … Parkway strips will be installed as natural turf including City designated tree(s) … In the event the owner wishes to xeriscape the parkway strip, approval of the DRC is required prior to installation. Xeriscape plans must follow the guidance from the City of Fort Collins. Once approved by the DRC, the owner must also receive parkway landscape amendment approval from the City of Fort Collins prior to installation
source_label: Waters Edge Metropolitan District Design Guidelines (Sonders Fort Collins), Sec. III.j Landscaping

fact: Waters Edge requires approval for outdoor lighting, which must aim down and keep its light on the lot, with walkway lights no taller than 24 inches and landscape lighting off between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.
quote: Approval from the DRC is required prior to installation … Any exterior lighting, including any security type fixtures and home/dwelling accent lighting must be directed downwards and the light “cone” created must be contained within the property boundaries to avoid a glare source to neighboring properties … • Walkway lighting must be directed to the ground and not exceed twenty-four (24) inches in height • Landscape lighting must be placed on a timer, switch, or otherwise be programmable to not illuminate between 10:00 pm and 6:00 am
source_label: Waters Edge Metropolitan District Design Guidelines (Sonders Fort Collins), Sec. III.k Lighting

fact: Waters Edge's guidelines allow rear- and side-yard accent fencing only as a black, 4-foot, 3-rail Ameristar Montage Majestic metal fence set at least 4 feet behind the front wall of the home, with a 6-foot solid fence allowed along the alleys of alley-load courtyard homes.
quote: Homeowners are allowed to install 4-foot tall, 3-rail Ameristar Montage Majestic Metal Fence accent fencing around the rear and side yards of their homes • In addition, alley load courtyard homes may use a 6’ solid fence for security in the alleys, which must be stained or sealed in colors approved by the DRC • All wing fencing must be installed a minimum of four (4) feet behind the front wall of the home … • All accent fencing must be black 4-foot tall, 3-rail Ameristar Montage Majestic Iron Fence, installed per manufacturer’s instructions
source_label: Waters Edge Metropolitan District Design Guidelines (Sonders Fort Collins), Sec. III.g Fencing

fact: A Waters' Edge Metropolitan District No. 1 resolution effective November 15, 2023 gives a first owner 90 days after a closing between March 31 and August 15 to install landscaping the builder did not, or 90 days after the next April 1 for other closings, with plans approved by the Design Review Committee first.
quote: The First Amendment shall be effective as of November 15, 2023. … To the extent landscaping has not been installed by the applicable Builder, the first owner of each Lot shall install landscaping on such Lot within ninety (90) days after acquisition of such Lot, if the closing occurs between March 31 and August 15. If closing occurs between August 15 and March 31, of any year, landscaping is to be installed within ninety (90) days after the April 1 immediately following the closing. Landscaping plans must be approved by the DRC prior to landscaping installation.
source_label: Resolution of the Board of Directors of Waters' Edge Metropolitan District No. 1 Adopting an Amendment to the Sonders Fort Collins Design Guidelines (Landscape Installation Timeline, 2023), Exhibit A
notes: Scanned PDF; read from the page images 2026-09-26. The posted design guidelines (Sec. III.j) and the recorded Declaration (Sec. 6.2) still carry the older March 31 / September 1 window: see fort-collins-co--waters-edge.dg-landscape-timeline-posted. The page says the documents disagree and sends owners to the DRC.

fact: The design guidelines the Waters' Edge district posts still give a first owner 90 days after a closing between March 31 and September 1 to install landscaping the builder did not, or 90 days after the next April 1 for other closings, the same window as the recorded Declaration.
quote: To the extent landscaping has not been installed by the applicable Builder, the first owner of each Lot shall install landscaping on such Lot within ninety (90) days after acquisition of such Lot, if the closing occurs between March 31 and September 1. If closing occurs between September 1 and March 31, of any year, landscaping is to be installed within ninety (90) days after the April 1 immediately following the closing
source_label: Waters Edge Metropolitan District Design Guidelines (Sonders Fort Collins), Sec. III.j Landscaping
notes: Declaration Sec. 6.2(a) (Larimer County Reception No. 20220024320) uses the same March 31 / September 1 window. Conflicts with the 2023 resolution (August 15).

fact: The recorded Sonders Fort Collins Declaration says landscaping must be finished within 30 days of starting, that landscaping plans must be professionally done and approved by the Design Review Committee before installation, and that a request for a variance goes to the metro district rather than the committee.
quote: Landscaping of a Lot must be completed within thirty (30) days after an Owner commences such landscaping. (b) Landscaping plans and other required documents shall be professionally done, shall be in accordance with the Guidelines and applicable governmental landscape standards, if any, and shall be submitted to the DRC for review, and the approval of the same shall be obtained prior to the installation of landscaping, except where installed by the Declarant or Builder. … If any Owner is applying for a variance to the Restrictions or the Guidelines, such application must be submitted to the Metropolitan District, not the DRC, for review and consideration.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Sonders Fort Collins, Secs. 6.2 and 6.4 (Larimer County Reception No. 20220024320, recorded April 15, 2022)
notes: Scanned recorded document with an OCR layer; wording checked against the pdftotext output, with OCR slips ("govemmental", "thi11y") read as the printed words.

fact: The Sonders Fort Collins Declaration has owners agree not to install landscaping, earth berms, walls or other improvements that change a lot's grading, and requires a plan approved by the Design Review Committee before a lot's established drainage is changed.
quote: Each Owner shall maintain the grading upon such Owner's Lot at the slope and pitch fixed by the final grading thereof, including landscaping and maintenance of the slopes. … if it is necessary or desirable to change the established drainage over any Lot which an Owner has a duty to maintain, then the party responsible for the maintenance of such real property shall submit a plan to the DRC for its review and approval … each Owner covenants and agrees: (a) Not to install Improvements, including, but not limited to, landscaping, items related to landscaping, earth berms, walls, walks, driveways, parking pads, patios, fences, Residence, additions to a Residence, outbuildings, or any other item or improvement which will change the grading of the Lot.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Sonders Fort Collins, Secs. 8.20 and 9.4(a) (Larimer County Reception No. 20220024320)

fact: The Sonders Fort Collins Declaration keeps turf grass, flower beds and vegetable gardens at least 5 feet from a home's foundation and slabs, asks owners to minimize sprinkler piping within 5 feet of foundation walls, and bars gravel beds that pond water and any polyethylene moisture barrier under gravel.
quote: (d) Not to plant turf grass, flower beds (especially annuals) or vegetable gardens adjacent to or within five (5) feet of the foundation and slabs of a Residence. (e) To minimize the installation of piping and heads for sprinkler systems within five (5) feet of foundation walls and slabs. (f) To install any gravel beds in a manner which will assure that water will not pond in the gravel areas, whether due to non-perforated edging or due to installation of the base of the gravel bed at a level lower than the adjacent lawn. (g) Not to install a moisture barrier (such as polyethylene) under any gravel.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Sonders Fort Collins, Sec. 9.4(d) to (g), Drainage and Soils Conditions (Larimer County Reception No. 20220024320)
notes: "Turf grass" here is live grass; the Declaration does not mention artificial turf.

fact: On the Waters Edge design review request form, the owner acknowledges that district approval is not a City building permit and that no change in drainage or elevation is allowed unless the committee expressly approves it, and is told to follow up if no receipt notice arrives within seven days.
quote: I also understand that the approval does not constitute approval by the City’s building department and that a Building Permit may be required. I agree to complete all proposed improvements promptly after receiving approval. I understand that any change in drainage and elevation is not permitted unless expressly approved by the DRC. … If you have not received written notice confirming receipt of this application within seven days following submission, please contact Kaitlin Frey, Waters’ Edge Metropolitan District
source_label: Waters' Edge Metropolitan District No. 1, Design Review Request Form, as posted on the district's Design Guidelines page
notes: The form also says a change in drainage and elevation may affect builder warranties; left out of the page's copy.

provider: Waters' Edge Metropolitan District No. 1 (non-potable irrigation)
fact: Waters' Edge Metropolitan District No. 1 runs a non-potable irrigation system supplied by ELCO under an annual allotment of 15,589,000 gallons for its service area, and owners must connect their sprinkler systems to it and build them for water that may carry particulate matter.
quote: The Non-Potable Water for the Irrigation System is supplied by ELCO. The annual allotment for the District’s Service Area is 15,589,000 gallons per year. … To the extent practicable, all outside irrigation of Landscaping shall use water from the Irrigation System. Owners shall be required to connect sprinkler and irrigation systems to the Irrigation System. All automatic sprinkler and irrigation systems shall be equipped and designed for use with the Irrigation System, which may contain particulate matter or other foreign substances from time to time.
source_label: Waters' Edge Metropolitan District No. 1, Rules and Regulations for Irrigation System (approved June 27, 2024), Secs. 1.1 and 4.1

provider: Waters' Edge Metropolitan District No. 1 (non-potable irrigation)
fact: Before new landscaping or replacing a significant part of it, a Waters Edge owner must give the district a Notice of Installation, the completed design review request form, at least 2 business days ahead, and neither the owner nor a contractor may shut off or turn on the irrigation system without the district's written permit.
quote: Notice of Installation – Shall mean the completed Design Review Request Form, available on the District’s website, to be submitted to the District Manager … When an Owner intends to install new Landscaping or replace a significant portion of the Landscaping on the Owner’s Property, the Owner must provide the District with a Notice of Installation at least 2 business days’ prior to commencement of the work. The Owner must coordinate with the District’s Consultants if the Irrigation System needs to be shut off or turned on in conjunction with the installation of Landscaping. No Owner, nor any contractor engaged by an Owner, is permitted to shut off or turn on the Irrigation System without written permit from the District.
source_label: Waters' Edge Metropolitan District No. 1, Rules and Regulations for Irrigation System (approved June 27, 2024), Secs. 2.16 and 4.5.1.2

provider: Waters' Edge Metropolitan District No. 1 (non-potable irrigation)
fact: Waters Edge irrigation runs on a schedule of three nights a week in 3-hour windows set by color-coded area, stops automatically after more than a quarter inch of rain, and is winterized centrally by the district, with spring start-up targeted for the first or second week of April.
quote: Blue 9:00pm-12:00am Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday … Green 3:00am-6:00am Monday, Wednesday, Friday … Owners may only use the Irrigation System for irrigation during the windows set forth in the Watering Schedule above. … In the event that the rain sensors for the Irrigation System determine that more than one quarter of an inch of rain has fallen, the Watering Schedule will be automatically suspended. … The Irrigation System is constructed for centralized winterization and spring activation. … Spring activation is targeted for the first or second week of April each year, weather permitting.
source_label: Waters' Edge Metropolitan District No. 1, Rules and Regulations for Irrigation System (approved June 27, 2024), Secs. 4.5.1 and 4.5.2, Table 1
notes: Table 1 has six colors: Blue, Orange and Pink water Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday; Yellow, Purple and Green Monday, Wednesday and Friday, each in one of three 3-hour windows between 9 p.m. and 6 a.m.

fact: The Waters' Edge district provides irrigation water only, ELCO provides drinking water, and the Richards Lake Master Association manages the lake amenity.
quote: The District provides irrigation water only. Potable (drinking) water service is provided by East Larimer County Water District (ELCO). … Management of the water amenity is provided by Richards Lake Master Association
source_label: Waters' Edge Metropolitan District Nos. 1–5, New Resident Info page

fact: The Sonders FAQ says the metro district funds landscape maintenance and non-potable irrigation for tree lawns and front yards, but not flower and planting beds on private lots or any rear-yard improvements.
quote: Landscape maintenance for homeowners for tree lawns and front yards (excluding flower and planting beds on private lots, and any rear yard improvements). Non-potable irrigation for tree lawn and front yard utilizing the community’s water-wise open space irrigation systems. A spring fertilization and aeration, weekly mowing, and monthly edging.
source_label: Sonders Fort Collins, Frequently Asked Questions about Sonders Fort Collins (April 28, 2022)
notes: A developer's FAQ, not a governing document; the recorded Declaration (Sec. 5.2) gives the district the right to maintain front grass and front landscaping.

fact: The 2022 Sonders FAQ put the community at about 375 homes of single-family, courtyard, townhome, condominium and custom types, all inside the Waters' Edge metro districts.
quote: There will be approximately 375 homes at Sonders according to current development plans. … Upon completion, there will be an array of housing types including single-family, courtyard, townhomes, condominiums and custom homes. … The official name of the Sonders Fort Collins Metropolitan District is “Waters’ Edge Metro Districts 1-2” and includes all of the homes, townhomes, and future condominiums at Sonders.
source_label: Sonders Fort Collins, Frequently Asked Questions about Sonders Fort Collins (April 28, 2022)
notes: The district's own site now names Waters' Edge Metropolitan District Nos. 1–5, with Nos. 3–5 inactive since December 4, 2020 (2025 Consolidated Annual Report).

fact: The Sonders builder design guidelines cap turf grass at 25% of the landscape area on courtyard-home lots, 45% on patio-home lots and 60% on single-family and custom-home lots, require other landscape areas to reach 50% plant coverage within 3 years, and tie all irrigation to the non-potable system.
quote: The maximum amount of turf grass shall be as noted below: Courtyard Homes (lots 280-329 - 25% of landscape area Patio Home Lots (lots 1-14, 120-136, 177-279) - 45% of landscape area Single Family Lots (lots 97-119, 137-151, 153-176) - 60% of landscape area Custom Homes … - 60% of landscape area … All landscape areas that are not turf grass shall be planted with a combination of shrubs, ornamental grasses, perennials, or similar material to achieve a minimum of 50% overage of the landscape area within 3 years of planting. … Non-potable water irrigation is provided to all lots. All landscape areas shall be installed with an automatic irrigation system that is connected to the non-potable water irrigation system.
source_label: Sonders Fort Collins Architectural Design Guidelines for builders (October 2021), Landscaping Requirements, posted on the district's District Documents page
notes: "overage" is the document's own word (read: coverage). The Sonders Custom Homes Design Guidelines (November 2022) carry the same 60% cap for custom lots. "Turf grass" means live grass; neither document says how artificial turf counts.

fact: In Larimer County's platted-lot map, the 247 numbered lots of the Waters Edge 2nd Filing measure about 5,400 to 13,200 square feet with a median near 6,250, and the 78 lots of the 3rd Filing about 2,700 to 3,400 square feet.
quote: SUBNAME: WATERS EDGE 2ND · SUBNUM: 8268002000 … SUBNAME: WATERS EDGE 3RD · SUBNUM: 8268003000

Lots labelled 142 to 152 in the 2nd Filing, the lot numbers the builder guidelines give the custom homesites, run 9,564 to 13,204 sq ft (the match between plat labels and guideline lot numbers is an inference: both run 1 to 329).

fact: Larimer County's subdivision records place the Waters Edge 2nd and 3rd filings inside the City of Fort Collins.
quote: SUBNAME: WATERS EDGE 2ND · SUBMJRNAME: WATERS EDGE · RECEPTNUM: 20180033452 · MUNICIPALITY: FORT COLLINS … SUBNAME: WATERS EDGE 3RD · SUBMJRNAME: WATERS EDGE · RECEPTNUM: 20200084218 · MUNICIPALITY: FORT COLLINS
source_label: Larimer County parcel GIS, Subdivisions layer: Waters Edge 2nd and 3rd filings
notes: A 'WATERS EDGE 1ST' in the same layer is in Loveland and is a different subdivision. The two Fort Collins filings sit near 40.628 N, 105.045 W, by Richards Lake.

fact: The Sonders community map describes The Greens as a neighborhood park with putting greens and chipping areas.
quote: The Greens If “practice makes perfect” then here’s the perfect place to practice. Putting greens, and chipping areas in a neighborhood, park-like setting.
source_label: Sonders Fort Collins, Interactive Community Map (The Greens card)
notes: The developer's site says planned amenities are subject to change; whether The Greens is built was not checked. The 2022 FAQ calls it a park with gathering areas around putting greens for practice. Surface (natural or synthetic) not stated.

fact: Richards Lake is a private lake, primarily a water-storage facility managed by the Water Supply and Storage Company of Fort Collins, that only residents of the Richards Lake neighborhood and Sonders and their guests may use.
quote: Richard’s Lake is a private lake with no access for the general public. Only residents of the Richard’s Lake neighborhood and Sonders Fort Collins, along with their guests, are permitted to use the lakefront and lake surface. … The lake is primarily a water storage facility managed by the Water Supply and Storage Company of Fort Collins.
source_label: Sonders Fort Collins blog, Another Lakefront Retreat for Sonders Residents: Richard's Lake (September 16, 2024)

fact: Sonders describes itself as sitting alongside Fort Collins Country Club, five miles north of Old Town Fort Collins.
quote: Nestled alongside Fort Collins Country Club, … and five miles north of Old Town Fort Collins is our burgeoning collection of new neighborhoods that are innovative and uniquely livable.
source_label: Sonders Fort Collins, Location page
